ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, C, and D are on the circle $\odot O$, with $\angle AOC=140^\circ$. Point B is the midpoint of the arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$. What is the degree measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line OB as shown in the figure,\\
since point B is the midpoint of $\widehat{AC}$, and $\angle$AOC=$140^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$AOB=$\frac{1}{2}\angle$AOC=$70^\circ$,\\
by the Inscribed Angle Theorem, we have $\angle$D=$\frac{1}{2}\angle$AOB=$\boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O; A, B, C, and D are all on the circumference; A is above, B is on the right side, C is on the lower right, and D is on the left side. Two chords DA and DB are drawn from D, and ∠D in the figure denotes ∠ADB. Reasoning: The problem gives ∠AOC=140°, so the corresponding arc AC is 140°. B is the midpoint of arc AC, therefore arc AB is half of arc AC, namely 70°. ∠ADB intercepts arc AB; according to the inscribed angle theorem, ∠D=∠ADB=1/2×70°=35°.
